what: Round 2, second PR, of the C++ core port of the web-only style passes (ADR 0019): hysteresis quantisation (decisions that remember the previous frame), palette-locked lighting, and palette dither. Same links as evidence/cpp-port-style-bounds.json: JavaScript float64 against C++ float64 (CPU link), and C++ float64 against the one WGSL source on D3D12 (WARP) and WebGPU (SwiftShader). Each section is committed before the first run of the code it bounds; the dither section is added in its own commit before dither's first run.
rules: As evidence/cpp-port-style-bounds-2.json: built-in controls that must fail on every run; one hand edit of a constant in the C++ and one in style.wgsl per pass, run, recorded in evidence/cpp-port-style-runs-3.json and reverted; software adapters only (RAW_NATIVE_D3D12_WARP=1 on every D3D12 command); codeStats over RGB.

hysteresis.written: 2026-10-16, before the C++ reference, the WGSL rewrite and the first run
hysteresis.fixtures: The three cases of evidence/shaders-hysteresis-parity-bounds.json at 320 x 200: bands6 and pico8 over 12 frames of the street lamp flicker (t = f / 24), and bands6 over 8 frames of a camera orbit with motion vectors (web/shaders/hysteresis/sequences.mjs). Frames, motion vectors and view distances are exported as the f32 arrays the web page feeds both implementations; the JavaScript step() runs the sequence and its decisions and RGBA8 codes are exported per frame.
hysteresis.previous_frame: Both C++ paths carry the state between frames: the CPU reference as a decision, count and distance per pixel; the GPU path as two state buffers swapped each frame, the previous frame's read and this frame's written, as web/shaders/hysteresis/gpu.mjs does.

cpu_link.tie_excuse: A decision mismatch is excused only where one of the C++ decision quantities (the band coordinate L N against a rounding edge or a keep-interval edge; a palette distance against the nearest or the keep margin; the persistence count is an integer) is within 1e-9 of its threshold; at most 2 excused a case over all its frames.
cpu_link.code_mismatch_where_decisions_agree: 0, except at an 8-bit rounding edge within 1e-9 (counted with the excused ties)

gpu_link.why: The web parity bounds: a decision flips only within f32 rounding of a threshold or margin edge, and hysteresis can carry a flip to later frames.

controls.built_in: the C++ reference with the margin raised by 0.1: must give at least one decision mismatch on the CPU link and exceed max_decision_mismatch_fraction on the GPU link, on every case
controls.source_edit: C++ and, separately, WGSL: the 0.5 of the bands keep interval [p - 0.5 - m, p + 0.5 + m] to 0.45. Prediction: the CPU link fails on the two bands cases and passes on the palette case; WARP fails on at least bands-flicker.

palettelight.written: 2026-10-16, before the C++ reference, the WGSL rewrite and the first run
palettelight.fixtures: The five cases of evidence/shaders-palettelight-parity-bounds.json: Chapel Yard G-buffers from web/shaders/fixtures/chapel-render.mjs at 192 x 108 (f32 G-buffer, the same for every implementation), with each case's lamp position, time, plan overrides and camera.
palettelight.palette: The C++ builds the ramp palette itself (a port of web/shaders/palettelight/palette.mjs on the core's OKLab); the CPU link requires every entry's 8-bit sRGB to equal the JavaScript palette's, and the ramp tables to be equal.

cpu_link.tie_excuse: An index mismatch is excused only where a decision quantity (a ramp fraction or cycle phase against its Bayer threshold, the warm fraction against 0.3, 0.7 or its threshold) is within 1e-9 of its threshold; at most 2 a case.

gpu_link.why: The web parity bounds: an index flips only where a coordinate sits within f32 rounding of a threshold, and a flip moves one pixel to a neighbouring entry.

controls.built_in: the C++ reference with the tone gain multiplied by 1.1: must give index mismatches on the CPU link and exceed max_decision_mismatch_fraction on the GPU link, on every case
controls.source_edit: C++ and WGSL: the ambient constant 0.7 in ambient (0.7 + 0.3 (0.5 + 0.5 n.y)) to 0.75. Prediction: the CPU link fails on every case; WARP fails on at least one case.

addendum_a.written: 2026-10-16, after the first CPU-link run of hysteresis and palettelight, and before any GPU-link run
addendum_a.finding: The hysteresis built-in control as first written (the margin raised by 0.1) did not fail on bands-flicker: the CPU link matched the JavaScript on every decision and code of every case (0 mismatches, 0 ties), and so did the control on that case. A probe of the JavaScript reference shows why: over the 12 flicker frames the reference holds 7,727 decisions at margin 0.3 and the same 7,727 at margin 0.4, so a wider margin changes nothing on this sequence. The control on palette-flicker and bands-orbit failed as required.
addendum_a.change: The hysteresis built-in control on both links becomes the margin set to 0, which turns the hysteresis off (a decision is kept only inside its own plain interval). On bands-flicker that changes 7,727 of 768,000 decisions (1.0%), above the GPU bound of 2e-4. The rule that a run whose control passes fails as a whole is unchanged, and so is every bound.
addendum_a.unchanged: Every bound, case, tie rule, the palettelight controls and the source-edit controls.
